title: Sample satellite files at points or over areas

ports.note: Takes the places to read at, one kind of the three: points, a polygon layer, or a study area's units; and the files a search kept. Emits a long table: for points, one row per point per overpass or period; for areas, one row per area per period per satellite, with the cells counted.

ontology.note: The receipt states the route, the variable, the unit as the file states it, the pixel convention, the quality variable, threshold and operator, files read, points, rows written, and rows passing, below the threshold, with no retrieval and with no overpass; fw:completenessRead true and fw:imputed false. Held by fw:SatellitePointSampleShape. Over areas, or at points in a gridded file: fw:SatelliteAreaSample, with the cell convention, the quality rule in words, places sampled and rows with no cell, held by fw:SatelliteAreaSampleShape. And fw:filesFromDevice, how many of the files were taken from readings saved on this device by an earlier run.

changes.description: Keeps what it reads on this device (the practitioner, 2026-11-09: "needs to be able to cache the satellite data read to save time"): each file's reading at the places, a few numbers per place, in IndexedDB, keyed by the file, layer, quality rule, places and reader version. A file read before the same way is not read again, after a reload or another day; the result and the receipt (fw:filesFromDevice) say how many. Configure… reads every file again on the next run, or forgets every saved reading. On the standard Inspector and dialog (experiment 186): the name, its inputs, one sentence and Configure…, where the layer, quality rule, unit, place column or qa_value operator are set, and what the last run read.

evidence.note: Lab check 35 holds the point reading of Sentinel-5P against h5py and pyproj (0.2.1). The area reading has unit tests, an offline browser test with three areas, and a run in Node over the 92 Rio de Janeiro municipalities against real MODIS files (experiment 180, M2); no lab check yet.
